name: Amazigh
description: The Amazigh people, also known as Berber, are an ethnic group from North Africa. Their strong sense of identity clashes with the Arabic invaders that have been shaping their home regions since centuries ago.

name: Andean
description: Living in or near the Andes, the people of this mountainous region are adapted to a lifestyle that is well suited for the many different climates and terrain of the highlands. This common lifestyle connects the rich cultures and civilizations of the Andes.

name: Arabian
description: The lands of the Arabian Peninsula are populated by a diverse group of people. From the highlands of Yemen to the oases of the central lands these people have adapted to harsh environments and conditions.

name: Arabic
description: Since the rise and fall of the Umayyad Caliphate most of the peoples that were under its rule have retained much of their influence and culture even long after its disappearance.

name: Austroasiatic
description: One of the oldest cultural groups in Asia, the $austroasiatic_group$ peoples have developed an array of societies that go from very advanced empires to underdeveloped jungle warring tribes.

name: Austronesian
description: As one of the most widespread cultural and linguistic families, the $austronesian_group$ peoples have populated lands from Madagascar to Easter Island. They have been considered excellent seafarers and brought technologies and animals with them in their colonial efforts.

name: Baltic
description: The Baltic peoples are those living on the southeastern coast of the Baltic Sea. Originally mainly from the same branch that gave rise to the Slavic peoples, they were already differentiated by the times of the Roman Empire. Over the centuries, interaction with different Germanic peoples, as well as groups of Slavs, created a unique identity. Not only the original Baltic-speaking peoples, still keeping their original religion, but also the many groups of Christian German peoples living on those shores can now be called Baltic.

name: Bohemian
description: The Lands of the Bohemian Crown were populated mainly by different Slavic peoples. However, being not only inside the Holy Roman Empire but one of its biggest constituents, they were also very influenced by German culture and traditions. On top of that, a lot of German settlers were attracted to the lands of Bohemia, which further expanded such influence.

name: British
description: Britannia is called home by many people, its prehistoric makeup disturbed by waves of migration from the Celtic tribes, the Roman Empire, the Germanic world, Ireland, and France. Physical separation from the continent unites all the peoples of their isle.

name: Carpathian
description: The rugged arcs of the Carpathian Mountains have long shaped the lives of those who dwell among their ridges and valleys. Isolated communities adapted to shifting borders and empires, developing a resilience tied to the land itself. Mountain passes and highland fortresses fostered trade and defense alike.

name: Caucasian
description: Where Europe and Asia meet, the Caucasus rises as a land of peaks and narrow valleys. Its sheer landscapes shields fiercely independent peoples, while its mountain passes drew the ambitions of empires...

name: Celtic
description: The Celts, a patchwork of peoples who once stretched from Iberia to Anatolia, lie reduced along the harsh Atlantic coastline, pushed to the craggy fringes of Europe by centuries of invasion and settlement.

name: Chinese
description: China has been broken apart and reunified multiple times over the centuries, but the idea of it has never ceased to exist. Despite being very diverse in terms of culture and language, the many different peoples living in it all share the concept of being inherently Chinese, inhabitants and custodians of the Middle Kingdom.

name: Confucian-Influenced
description: A collection of cultures which have been directly or indirectly influenced by the ideas and morals of Confucianism.

name: Dravidian
description: Concentrated in the southern third of India, the $dravidian_group$ people are the descendants of the natives of the subcontinent before the $indo_aryan_group$ invasions. While these invaders culture eventually permeated $dravidian_group$'s, they have maintained strong regional identities.

name: Tibeto-Burman
description: Migrations from the Tibetan plateau during the earlier historic periods brought these peoples to several places, including India. Their development has been unequal, though, with some groups developing advanced and complex societies, while others have remained rather tribal.

name: Ethiopian
description: The ancient kingdom of Axum brought the people of Ethiopia in contact with the Mediterranean world through Egypt, having trade with Greece and the Roman Empire, and it also brought Christianity. However, after the rise of Islam, the Ethiopians saw themselves cut from that contact and somewhat isolated as the only group of Christian Semitic peoples. This created a shared heritage that survives despite the cultural differences among themselves.

name: Finnic
description: The Finnic peoples are living on both sides of the Gulf of Finland. While their strong identity remains intact, they have been under threat of invasion both from scandinavian and german people.

name: French
description: Having its origins in the Germanic Franks that occupied the area after the fall of the Roman Empire, the Kingdom of France later expanded to include other peoples besides them. Despite their differences in customs and languages, all these peoples share the identity of being French.

name: German
description: Rooted in a rich tapestry of ancient tribes, the Germanic peoples entered history as sometimes rivals, sometimes allies of the Roman Empire. As the centuries passed, Charlemagne's Empire and Feudalism shaped their identity, developing into the creation of the Holy Roman Empire.

name: Swiss
description: The Swiss are the people who call the Swiss Plateau and the Alps their home. Due to their geographical position, the Swiss group is not exclusively Germanic as French and Italian cultures are part of Switzerland.

name: Roman
description: The Latins and Hellenes, pioneers of democracy and philosophy, shaped Western civilization with their enduring cultural and intellectual legacy. From epic poetry to classical architecture, their contributions resonate through millennia.

name: Haudenosaunee
description: The Haudenosaunee are a diverse group of peoples, but all of them united not only by linguistic similarities but also by their shared sense of community, cooperation, and core beliefs, which are expressed in the many ways their peoples tend to organize themselves together.

name: Hibernian
description: The Emerald Isle was originally inhabited by the Gaels, but conquests and settlements have brought many newcomers from Britain and the continent. Even those of foreign ancestry may feel compelled to answer Ireland's call.

name: Magyar
description: The Magyar, or Hungarians, are a group of people originating in the area of the Southern Urals that moved gradually westwards pushed by (and getting influence from) other peoples of the steppes, like the Huns, Avars, Bulgars, and Turks, until they settled in the Carpathian Basin after the fall of the Avar Khaganate. This makes them quite different from the rest of their European neighbors, which only contributes to their sense of unity.

name: Iberian
description: The Iberian Peninsula, a land of contrasts and rich history, is home to diverse peoples. The ancient Celts, Iberians, and Basques have been influenced by the Phoenicians, Romans, Visigoths, and Moors. Several distinct identities have merged forging a unique blend of Christian, Muslim, and Jewish cultures. From the vibrant courts of the south to the heroic knights of the north, the Iberian peoples embody a complex tapestry of traditions and aspirations.

name: Indian
description: 'Indian' is an umbrella term referring to the vast and diverse cultures that reside on the subcontinent of India. Although each culture is unique and languages are plentiful, the shared geography and distinct separation through natural borders in every direction creates a shared history for these cultures.

name: Indic Diaspora
description: The Indic Diaspora encompasses nomadic communities originating in North West India, who have migrated across various regions including the Middle East and Europe. These groups, while retaining elements of their Indian heritage, have adapted to diverse cultures and environments.

name: Indo-Aryan
description: The descendants of the Indo-European people that invaded the Indian Subcontinent, these people became the dominant population in the northern areas. Their settlement shaped early Vedic culture and laid the base for a myriad of languages and empires.

name: Iranian
description: The cultures of Iran are ancient and have a long and complicated origin. The Iranians in the Persia region are the descendants of Western Iranian peoples who ruled over the Middle East like the Achaemenid Empire and Sasanian Empire. After the Muslim conquest of Persia, Islam has become a major pillar of Iranian culture.

name: Italian
description: Italy, a vibrant patchwork of realms and city-states, is a melting pot of cultures and influences. From the ancient Romans to the Byzantines, Lombards, and Normans, various peoples have left their mark on the Italian Peninsula. Italians compete fiercely for power and prestige, fostering a flourishing culture and artistic patronage.

name: Japanese
description: The people of Japan have inhabited their islands ever since the mythical age of the gods and the first Japanese Emperor, Jinmu-tennō, according to their own narration of their history. Centuries of isolation interrupted by periodical contacts with the continent through Korea and China have made the Japanese into something distinct, and their unique language and native beliefs have no similarity to anything present on the continent. Although diverse among themselves, the Japanese people have developed a shared unique identity.

name: Jewish
description: The $jewish_group$ group refers to the different ethno-religious groups that follow the $jewish_group$ religion.

name: Jurchen
description: The $jurchen_group$ people, native to the rugged lands of Manchuria, are fierce warriors that forged the mighty Jīn Dynasty and destroyed the Khitan Liáo Dynasty during the 12th century. Masters of horsemanship and archery, they, who once shaped empires, continue to inspire with their resilience and rich heritage.

name: Lithuanian
description: Among the different Baltic Peoples, the Lithuanians have come together through similarities of language and common threats, forming together the Lithuanian state. Their pagan beliefs while being surrounded by hostile Christians on all fronts further increased their shared sense of unity.

name: Maghrebi
description: The special characteristics of the north of Africa, the many empires that have risen and fallen on its lands and its unique situation between the calm sea of the Mediterranean to the north and the unforgiving sea of dunes of the Sahara to the south, has created a group of cultures singularly adept on taking care of it.

name: Micronesian
description: As their Polynesian neighbors, the Micronesians excel at seafaring and have managed to colonize hundreds of islands and atolls across the Western Pacific.

name: Mongol
description: Originating from the vast steppes of Central Asia, the $mongolian_group$ people embody a nomadic legacy that spans centuries. Renowned for their equestrian prowess and skilled archery, they traverse the open plains, fostering a deep connection with their herds. Through the leadership of historic figures like $genghis_khan_name_no_tooltip$, they have forged one of the largest empires in history, leaving an indelible mark on the annals of conquest. Their enduring cultural richness encompasses traditions of horsemanship, throat singing, and a resilient spirit anchored in the boundless expanses they call home.

name: Nahua
description: The $nahua_culture$ that inhabit the region of Mexico are famed for their advanced societies, intricate government systems, and warlike relations with their neighbors.

name: Nepali
description: The people of the Nepal area are of diverse origins and heritages. While the Gurung and Tamang have their roots in China and Tibet, the Khas and Kumaoni hail from the Indian subcontinent. Nonetheless, the variety of cultures of Nepal claim the Himalayas as their home.

name: Netherlandish
description: In the low-lying lands marked by rivers and the perpetual struggle with the sea, the diverse Netherlandish people have forged a unique identity. Known for mercantile prowess, maritime exploration, and innovation, they share a common heritage shaped by trade and an unyielding mastery over their watery domain.

name: Polish
description: Divided among several countries after the fall of the last Polish State, the Polish people share a common western Slavic heritage and a strong Catholic Faith.

name: Polynesian
description: The people of Polynesia have always been seafarers, expanding all the many islands in the Pacific over the centuries. Despite being isolated from each other, the many groups living there still can trace their common cultural heritage and linguistic similarities.

name: Pueblo
description: Hailing from the fractured Ancestral Puebloans, the Pueblo people have since diverged into differing tribes across $shiewhibak_area$. Through the harsh lands of $shiewhibak_area$, the Pueblo people have grown resilient, and constructed sophisticated Adobe structures and irrigation systems.

name: Pyrenean
description: Born of the Pyrenees Mountains that separates southern France from Iberia, the Pyrenean people share a bond forged by the shared hardships and unique societal innovations of remote life in rough borderlands.

name: Romanian
description: The $romanian_group$ people, descendants of ancient Dacians and Romans, mostly inhabit the regions of Wallachia, Moldova, and Transylvania, but also across the Balkans. They boast a unique Romance variant surrounded by Slavic languages. They are celebrated for their resilience, and a love for folklore that reflects in their music, traditions, and celebrations.

name: East Slavic
description: The Rus' people trace their origins to the Varangians, Scandinavian seafarers and warriors who settled in the Russian region around the 9th century. Over time, the Rus' underwent a process of cultural fusion, blending Slavic traditions with Scandinavian influences. Proximity to the Byzantine Empire promoted cultural and economic exchanges, contributing to their unique culture with a diverse mix of art, architecture, and language.

name: Scandinavian
description: Scandinavia is home to a diverse array of peoples, shaped by a rich history of migration, trade, and cultural exchange. The different realms have developed unique identities while maintaining a sense of shared heritage. Renowned for their seafaring skills and vibrant trading networks, the Scandinavians are known for their prowess in seamanship and governance.

name: Scottish
description: The northern reaches of Britain have long been home to many peoples of diverse backgrounds; the native Picts and Cumbrians abandoned their old ways when they became absorbed into kingships of foreign Gaelic, Anglo-Saxon, and Viking origin. But in times of trial, they still unite against outsiders and become one people: the Scottish.

name: Slavic
description: The Slavic peoples, originating on the upper areas of the Vistula and Dnieper rivers in the times of the Roman Empire, expanded over centuries to occupy much of Eastern Europe. Despite being separated into different branches and forming many different states and kingdoms, their shared cultural ancestry remains.

name: South Slavic
description: The Southern Slavs are a diverse group, including several peoples in the Balkan Peninsula. These people share a Slavic heritage and their linguistic roots but have developed distinct cultures over centuries.

name: Tatar
description: The origin of the Tatar people can be traced to Turkic and Mongol ethnic groups of Central Asia and is broadly used to refer to nomadic tribes, such as the Volga and Crimean Tatars. Each subgroup has its own distinct history, language variations, and cultural traditions, and are mostly connected by Islam, reflecting the influence of Islamic cultures in the regions they inhabit.

name: Tibetan
description: As residents of the high plateaus of Tibet and the Himalayas Mountains, the Tibetan people are used to extreme climates and terrain.

name: Tungusic
description: Distributed through most of Manchuria and Eastern Siberia, the $tungusic_group$ peoples have traditionally lived from hunting and trading. Adapted to the harsh climates of their native lands, these groups have usually organized in clannic structures.

name: Turkic
description: The Turkic peoples have come a long way since they originated centuries ago in the steppes of Asia. Having expanded to cover territories from the Black Sea to the Mongolian Steppes and down into Persia, they have interacted with many other cultures and peoples, and have diverged themselves into many different groups, but the shared Turkic identity remains.

name: West African
description: Despite being very diverse in terms of culture, language, and even religion, the people living in West Africa and the Sahel, all have a shared set of traits and characteristics, fueled by centuries of interactions among themselves. The relatively difficult-to-traverse terrains of the Sahara desert to the north and the forest and jungles to the south have promoted a more horizontal contact between peoples, creating this shared identity.

name: Malagasy
description: The diverse people of the island of Madagascar trace their origin from the coast of Southeast Africa to the islands of Southeast Asia.

name: Thai
description: Since their origins in the Southern parts of China to their migrations and subsequent establishing in the Chao Phraya valley, the original Tai peoples have developed a unique identity, merging their original traditions with influences from Mon and Khmer peoples.

name: Shan
description: Although originally an exonym from the Burmese language to refer to a variety of different Tai peoples migrated to the area, and also a cognate of Siam, it has allowed these various Tai groups to develop a shared identity.

name: Rhaetian
description: The $rhaetian_group$ people are an ethnolinguistic group composed of three primary Alpine communities: the Romansh, Ladins, and Friulians. While they do not share a single political entity, they are unified by their descent from a common Vulgar Latin substrate mixed with ancient Rhaetian and Celtic influences.

name: Steppe Group
description: The $steppe_group$ is formed by various cultures belonging to the $mongolian_group$ and $tatar_group$ that live in the steppes of Eurasia.

name: Hmong-Mien
description: The Hmong-Mien peoples inhabit the highlands of southern China and Southeast Asia, speaking languages of the independent Hmong-Mien family unrelated to any of their neighbors. Known for their vibrant textile traditions and fierce independence, they have historically resisted assimilation into the lowland empires surrounding them.

name: Papuan
description: The Papuan peoples are the indigenous inhabitants of New Guinea and neighboring islands, speaking hundreds of languages from diverse and largely unrelated language families collectively known as Papuan. Their remarkable linguistic and cultural diversity reflects thousands of years of isolated development across the island's rugged terrain.

name: Atlantic
description: The Atlantic peoples of West Africa inhabit the coasts and savannas from Senegambia to Sierra Leone, speaking languages of the Atlantic branch of the Niger-Congo family. They include the great horsemen and traders of the Senegambian coast as well as the forest-dwelling Mel peoples of the Sierra Leone hinterland.

name: Kru
description: The Kru peoples of the Liberian and Ivorian coasts speak languages of the Kru branch of Niger-Congo and are renowned for their maritime skill and fierce resistance to enslavement. Their seafaring traditions made them valued sailors along the West African coast for centuries.

name: Kwa
description: The Kwa peoples of the Gold Coast and the Bight of Benin speak languages of the Kwa branch of Niger-Congo, encompassing the Akan states of the interior and the coastal Ewe and Fon kingdoms. Their societies are marked by matrilineal inheritance among the Akan and the powerful Vodun religious tradition among the Fon and Ewe.

name: Volta-Niger
description: The Volta-Niger peoples of the Nigerian region speak languages of the Volta-Niger branch of Niger-Congo and include some of the most populous and politically sophisticated societies in West Africa. The Yoruba city-states, the Igbo village republics, and the Benin Kingdom are among the most accomplished polities on the continent.

name: Bantu
description: The Bantu peoples form the largest linguistic grouping in sub-Saharan Africa, their expansion from a homeland near the Cameroon-Nigeria border carrying Bantu languages and agricultural practices across central, eastern, and southern Africa over three millennia. Today Bantu-speaking peoples inhabit almost the entire southern half of the continent.

name: Central African
description: The peoples of Central Africa inhabit the vast Congo Basin and surrounding highlands, speaking languages of the Adamawa, Ubangian, and related families. Their cultures are as diverse as the rainforests, savannas, and rivers they call home, ranging from the forest-dwelling Baka to the river traders of the great Congo tributaries.

name: Nilotic
description: The Nilotic peoples are the pastoralist and semi-pastoralist communities of the Nile Valley and the East African plains, speaking languages of the Nilotic branch of Nilo-Saharan. From the cattle-herding Maasai of the Rift Valley to the fishermen of the Sudd, they are united by age-grade social structures and a deep dependence on livestock.

name: Nilo-Saharan
description: The Nilo-Saharan peoples inhabit a broad belt stretching from the Sahara to the Ethiopian highlands, speaking languages of the diverse Nilo-Saharan family. They include the farmers of the Nuba Mountains, the merchants of the Darfur sultanates, and the nomads of the Saharan fringe.

name: Cushitic
description: The Cushitic peoples of the Horn of Africa and the Nile Valley speak languages of the Cushitic branch of the Afro-Asiatic family. They encompass the camel nomads of Somalia and the Ogaden, the highland farmers of the Ethiopian Rift Valley, and the ancient Beja of the Red Sea coast.

name: Khoisan
description: The Khoisan peoples of southern and eastern Africa are among the oldest surviving populations on Earth, speaking languages distinguished by their remarkable click consonants. They include the San hunter-gatherers of the Kalahari and the Khoikhoi herders of the Cape, peoples who inhabited southern Africa long before the Bantu expansion.

name: Permic
description: The Permic peoples of the Ural Mountains region speak languages of the Permic branch of the Uralic family, closely related to Finnish and Estonian. The Komi and Udmurt peoples have long inhabited the forests between the Volga and the Urals, trading furs with their Slavic and Tatar neighbors.

name: Mordvinic
description: The Mordvinic peoples of the middle Volga region speak languages of the Mordvinic branch of the Uralic family, forming one of the largest indigenous groups of European Russia. The Moksha and Erzya are closely related but speak distinct languages and maintain separate cultural identities.

name: Pama-Nyungan
description: The Pama-Nyungan peoples inhabit the vast majority of the Australian continent, speaking languages of the Pama-Nyungan family which covers roughly eighty percent of Australia's land area. Despite the enormous diversity within this family, these peoples share broad cultural patterns including complex kinship systems, the Dreaming cosmology, and hunter-gatherer subsistence.

name: Australian Aboriginal
description: The Aboriginal peoples of Australia are among the oldest continuous cultures on Earth, having inhabited the continent for at least sixty-five thousand years. Their deep connection to the land, expressed through the concept of the Dreaming, and their sophisticated ecological knowledge make them unique among the world's peoples.

name: Swahili Coast
description: The peoples of the Swahili Coast have developed a distinctive maritime civilization along the Indian Ocean shore of East Africa, blending Bantu agricultural traditions with the mercantile culture of Arab and Persian traders. Their coral-stone city-states from Mogadishu to Kilwa formed the African terminus of the great Indian Ocean trade network.

name: Great Lakes Kingdoms
description: The peoples of the African Great Lakes region have developed some of the most sophisticated state structures in sub-Saharan Africa, with hierarchical kingdoms centered on cattle wealth and hereditary kingship. From the Buganda kingdom on the northern shore of Lake Victoria to the terraced hills of Rwanda, these interlacustrine societies share a common political culture of tribute, royal courts, and clan organization.

name: East African Pastoralist
description: The pastoralist peoples of East Africa range across the great savannas and semi-arid plains from the Ethiopian highlands to the Tanzanian steppe, herding cattle, camels, and goats between seasonal pastures. Organized through age-grade warrior systems and lacking permanent territorial states, they form a cross-linguistic cultural world spanning Nilotic, Cushitic, and other language families.

name: Nguni
description: The Nguni peoples of southeastern Africa speak a cluster of closely related Bantu languages distinguished by their rich system of click consonants borrowed from neighboring Khoisan peoples. Organized around cattle wealth, age-grade systems, and powerful chieftaincies, the Nguni gave rise to the great Zulu and Xhosa nations that dominated the eastern coast of southern Africa.

name: Sotho-Tswana
description: The Sotho-Tswana peoples of the southern African highveld speak the closely related Sotho and Tswana languages and share a common heritage of nucleated village life, cattle-based wealth, and sophisticated iron-working traditions. Their large towns on the dry plateau interior were among the most populous settlements in pre-colonial southern Africa.

name: Shona
description: The Shona-speaking peoples of the Zimbabwe plateau and the Limpopo valley built one of Africa's most remarkable pre-colonial civilizations, centered on the great stone enclosures of Great Zimbabwe and its successor states. Their control of the gold trade routes to the Indian Ocean coast made them a commercial power whose wealth reached as far as China and Persia.

name: Kongo
description: The Kongo peoples of the lower Congo River basin and the Atlantic coast developed one of the most centralized states in sub-Saharan Africa, the Kingdom of Kongo, with a sophisticated bureaucracy, provincial governors, and an extensive currency system using nzimbu shells. Their early encounter with Portuguese traders in the late fifteenth century made the Kingdom of Kongo one of the first African polities to engage diplomatically with European powers as an equal.

name: Luba
description: The Luba and Lunda peoples of the Katanga plateau and the Kasai basin built an interconnected web of tributary empires that dominated the heart of Central Africa for centuries. The Luba Empire pioneered the Nilotic model of divine kingship in Central Africa, and the Lunda expansion carried their political system of appointed governors across a vast swathe of the continent from Angola to Zambia.

name: Chokwe
description: The Chokwe peoples of the Angolan plateau are renowned for their exceptional artistic traditions, particularly their masks and wood carvings, and for their role in the long-distance trade networks that connected the Atlantic coast to the Central African interior. Originally subjects of the Lunda Empire, they expanded dramatically in the nineteenth century to become one of the dominant peoples of the region.
